activity_records.description: Wire 5.3: activity record values, built from messages.json's messages, and the record keys they sit at under the fixed policy, blinded with their reader's naming key: alice's for payer_activity, bob's for payee_activity. Some members only some records carry: request_hash, billing_period and earlier_details only a period record, attempt_id and unrequested only the record of a payment without a request, allowance_id and reassociations only a payer's request record, and manual_only only a payer's request record or a payer's period record. accepted are records their reader binds at their keys; refused are the same records with a member where their binding and side don't allow it, which their reader refuses, and, last, alice's request records storing a request whose sender's certificate doesn't allow it (wire 5.2, the sender's side of check 8): messages.json label_rejections' request labelled shop2 from bob's hosted app, which holds only paykit_request:shop1, and messages.json's payment_request presented with documents.json's chat-only certificate of the shop's keys, at the keys their requests name. Appended after them, on payment evidence (wire 4.11): accepted, records whose receipt is of the stored proof's attempt, or of the record's attempt_id; refused, the same with a receipt of another attempt. Appended last, on the members only some records carry (wire 4.9, 5.3): accepted, a payer's request record of the recurring request with reassociations; alice's request record of the one-time request, manual_only; her request record of the recurring request, manual_only; her period record, manual_only; the period record whose proof names messages.json's period details, with later details, signed again by the shop a day later under another msg_id, in earlier_details; the same record without its proof, the later details in period_details and the earlier in earlier_details; the record of the payment without a request with unrequested.amount, the proof's; and that record with members its reader doesn't know, in the value, in unrequested and in the stored proof, which its writer keeps; and a reassociation from the February period of the recurring request signed again with its anchor at half a second past midnight, named by the second it starts in; refused, those members where the record's binding, side or request doesn't allow them, period details out of order or held twice, reassociations without allowance_id, naming it first or not strictly ascending, an unrequested.amount other than the stored proof's, and a reassociation naming a time that isn't a Billing Period start of the stored request, which periods name by their start cut to whole seconds (between two starts, before the first period, for the request signed again ending at its March period after its ends_at, and, for the request signed again anchored at half a second past midnight, the second before its February period, whose own second it accepts); and, last, a period record with manual_only false, which is true or absent. later_writes holds pairs of versions of one record, the version a reader holds (held) and a later write (value), both of which bind at record_key, with built_on_held true when the write builds on the held version (wire 5.3 "Seen roles", "Seen Allowance", "Seen marks"). On alice's request record of the recurring request with its February period attempted early: accepted, a reassociation from a period after every attempted period, and one from that period built on a later version that dropped it, which a reader holding the older version takes; refused, built on the held version, a reassociation from the attempted period and one from before it, since a period attempted early stays under the Allowance it was attempted under. Also refused, whatever the write builds on: a write dropping period details seen only in earlier_details. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

allowance_records.description: Wire 4.16, 5.4: allowances record values of alice's, built from binding_accepted's record and messages.json's Allowance messages, some signed again by their sender with refs or sides changed, at the record key binding_accepted gives. A response refers to the proposal; an end refers to the proposal and the stored acceptance; an end referring to the proposal alone is its sender's withdrawal, before any response; a rejected Allowance has no end; executor_app_id comes only in an acceptance, from the allower; conflicted is a second proposal under the record's allowance_id, from either side, with valid terms and another hash than the record's proposal, or, beside the record's response, a second acceptance or rejection from the proposal's recipient, referring to the proposal, with another hash than the record's response (spec 8.3). accepted are records a reader binds; refused are those it refuses, the last two records whose stored message check 10 drops: a rejection carrying executor_app_id, and a conflicting proposal whose terms aren't valid. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

description: Paykit's sealed record values (wire 5), sealed as the Switch's sealed values are (the Switch set's sealed.json) under alice's scope_key(2, "paykit_pay") from the Switch set's keys.json, with record keys blinded with alice's naming key. binding_accepted holds record values, as they are sealed, that a reader binds to their record keys, recomputed with alice's naming key (wire 5.4, 5.5): a payment_lists record, an allowances record and its allowance_ledgers record, checked against that allowances record. binding_rejections holds the same values at a wrong key or with a field that doesn't match, a list record whose payee isn't the identity that sent its list (bob's list, filed under payee alice at the key of alice and the shop's App ID) and an acceptance naming another Allowance, each of which a reader refuses. labelled is a payee record of a labelled request. activity_records holds activity records a reader binds, and the same records with a member their binding and side don't allow, which it refuses. allowance_records holds allowances records a reader binds or refuses by their messages' lifecycle.

labelled.description: Wire 5.1, 5.3: bob's payee_activity record of messages.json's payment_request_labelled, holding the request and alice's acceptance, under the labelled policy read_scope paykit_request:shop1, write_scopes [paykit_request:shop1], at the record key that policy's hash gives (identifiers.json), sealed with bob's label key for shop1 at data epoch 1 (keys.json sub_scope_keys) and AAD lp("pubky-switch/v1/sealed", identity, "paykit_request:shop1", record key). The paykit_request key and another label's key don't open it. rejections are records a reader refuses: a labelled policy must name the label of the request the record holds, and the fixed policy an unlabelled request; reason is the prototype's wording.
